metadata.prompt:
CHOSEN: Cascade delete approach

Rationale:
- User's primary pain point is inability to fix mistakes
- Requiring manual edge deletion first adds friction to an already frustrating situation
- Precedent: Most graph tools (Neo4j DETACH DELETE, etc.) support cascade
- Safe with --dry-run flag to preview what will be deleted

Implementation approach:
1. Validate node exists (helpful error if not)
2. Count edges for summary (both directions)
3. If dry_run, return count without deleting
4. Delete in dependency order:
   - Edges first (from_node_id OR to_node_id matches)
   - Context records
   - Session node associations
   - Set nullable FKs to NULL (don't delete sessions/commands/roadmap items)
   - Finally delete the node itself
5. Return DeleteSummary with node_title and edges_deleted

This approach:
- Fixes the user's immediate problem
- Doesn't orphan related data unexpectedly
- Preserves sessions/commands/roadmap items (just unlinks them)

title: Cascade delete: node deletion removes all connected edges automatically
